title: Bean seed, clear jar and kitchen roll for the germination journal
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Dissolving, separating and plants (Do All Solids Dissolve? and Allotment)
source: Seeded from science/y5 lesson 30 (Bean seed, clear jar and kitchen roll for the germination journal (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 30: Solutions: where does the solid go?. To understand that a dissolved solid is still there, and that dissolving is a reversible change

questions.q: 25 g of sugar dissolves in 200 g of water. Mass of the solution?
questions.model: Mass is kept. Add the solute and solvent: 200 + 25 = 225. So 225 g.

questions.q: In salty water, which is the solute?
Count how many level teaspoons of salt dissolve in half a cup of cold water before it is saturated. Record each spoon.
questions.a: Usually several teaspoons before some salt stays at the bottom
questions.model: Teacher adds the first teaspoon on camera, stirs for 30 seconds and ticks the table: 'spoon 1: all dissolved'.

questions.q: Label the solute, solvent and solution in your cup.
questions.a: Solute: salt; solvent: water; solution: salty water

questions.q: 300 g water + 45 g salt. Mass of solution? Why?
questions.a: 345 g: mass is conserved; nothing is lost when dissolving

questions.q: The liquid that does the dissolving is the...
Big question: what will 10 g of salt in 100 g of water weigh?
questions.a: 110 g, because the salt is still there.
